author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only page answers "which veterinarians hold this specialty": every specialty the clinic knows, by its stored name, with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name, all on one page and reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html renders a page listing every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it (owner-stated address).
Each veterinarian under a specialty is shown by full name, first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary" under radiology in the seeded data.
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page (seeded: James Carter, Sharon Jenkins).
All specialties render on one page; the page offers no division into pages and no page selector.
A veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them (seeded: Linda Douglas under dentistry and surgery) - PRD edge case 3.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed and is shown as held by none rather than left blank - PRD edge case 4.
Specialties appear alphabetically by name, and the veterinarians under each alphabetically by last name, then first name (seeded order: dentistry, radiology, surgery) - PRD edge case 5.
The page carries the site navigation to owner search and to the veterinarian directory like every other page (REQ-SYS-001), and no navigation entry or other page links to the specialty listing.

The page's wording follows the reader's language with no hard-coded text, and every piece of it exists in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002); stored specialty names are shown as stored, untranslated.
The page offers no form or action that adds, changes, or removes a veterinarian or a specialty (NG-2).
non_goals: Any navigation entry for the specialty listing, or any link to it from another page - owner decision (intake line 1); a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.
Adding, changing, or removing veterinarians or specialties - NG-2 unchanged (intake line 1).
Searching or filtering by specialty or veterinarian - NG-9 unchanged; the page is a full listing with no query input.
A machine-readable form of the specialty listing - the machine-readable veterinarian list (REQ-VET-002) was withdrawn as unwanted.
Any change to the existing veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001).
notes: Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log; skipped. Boundary check: no contradiction with NG-2 (read-only, owner-quoted), NG-9 (listing, not search), REQ-SYS-001 (the page carries the site navigation; nothing links to it, per intake decision 2), or REQ-LANG-002 (binds the page wording). No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Reversible decisions taken during scoping, since the owner said no further answer will come: PRD edge case 4 (an unheld specialty is listed and shown as held by none, mirroring REQ-VET-001) and edge case 5 (alphabetical order). Both are recorded as an Open Question in docs/prd.md, alongside the deferred visible entry point. The seeded data has no unheld specialty, so edge case 4 needs its own test data. The ubiquitous language needed no new term; the PRD uses Specialty and Veterinarian only. The provenance header now marks REQ-VET-003 as owner-stated rather than derived.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice fits the vet feature package using only In-force catalog patterns (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog); no new module, no ADR. Two small adjustments, recorded in docs/system-design.md § Contracts. (1) A second repository in the vet package, SpecialtyRepository, supplies every specialty the clinic knows. Edge case 4 needs specialties no veterinarian holds, and those cannot be derived from VetRepository. It mirrors the lookup-value precedent PetTypeRepository (one repository per persisted root, § Naming). VetRepository stays unchanged even though the prd-entry lists it: its existing cached findAll() supplies the veterinarians, and a specialty query on the vet repository would break one-repository-per-root. (2) A new immutable value object, SpecialtyListing (vet package), owns the listing's rules. It is built by one static factory from the full specialty collection and the full veterinarian collection. It lists every specialty in name order, each with its holding veterinarians in last-name-then-first-name order. A specialty no one holds keeps an empty holder list, a veterinarian with several specialties appears under each, and a veterinarian with none appears under none. Lists are unmodifiable copies. Per the Web controller row and Design Principle 4, the controller holds none of these rules. VetController gains one GET /specialties.html handler: it reads both repositories, builds the SpecialtyListing, adds it to the model, and returns vets/specialtyList. Invariants recorded in § Contracts: Specialty carries no association back to its veterinarians, and SpecialtyListing matches a veterinarian to a specialty by identifier, never by instance. Basis for the covering-pattern claims: grep over src (IntelliJ oracle not connected, so the weaker basis). PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes at PetTypeRepository.java:37, Vet.getSpecialties at Vet.java:60, VetController.showVetList at VetController.java:45, the layout menuItem call at fragments/layout.html:51.
integration_points: Binding, GET /specialties.html: the handler binds nothing. It takes no @RequestParam, @ModelAttribute, or path variable, only the Model, so no request-bound type exists and no @InitBinder disallow list applies (security-principles § Realization, mass-assignment row). A query string such as ?page=2 is ignored.

Repository boundary, SpecialtyRepository in VetControllerTests: a hand-written, fixed, in-memory double registered as a bean by a nested @TestConfiguration. It returns radiology, with the same id as the Helen Leary fixture's radiology but as a separate instance, plus one specialty no fixture veterinarian holds. No Mockito stub (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, hand-write mocks).

Repository boundary, VetRepository in VetControllerTests: the existing @MockitoBean and its @BeforeEach findAll() stub (VetControllerTests.java:76) serve the new tests unchanged. James Carter holds nothing and Helen Leary holds radiology. Add no new given(...) stubbing; a per-test restub is a new framework stub this block does not sanction.
No boundary in SpecialtyListingTests: plain unit tests on real Vet and Specialty instances, with no Spring context and no doubles (testing-principles § Test Pyramid, unit layer).
Framework transport: MockMvc through the existing @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) slice, the one sanctioned mock (testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Template: vets/specialtyList.html enters fragments/layout with a menu value no nav item uses, so the site navigation renders and no entry is highlighted. fragments/layout.html and every other template stay unchanged, so nothing links to the page (REQ-SYS-001, intake decision 2).

Native image: PetClinicRuntimeHints registers method-invocation reflection for SpecialtyListing and its per-specialty element type, since only the template reads them reflectively. That registrar in the root package is the caller that justifies making both types public (architecture-principles Design Principle 5).

patterns.description: Lookup-value repository precedent for SpecialtyRepository. Unlike it, SpecialtyRepository needs no ORDER BY, because SpecialtyListing owns the ordering rule in one place. Keep it read-only with @Transactional(readOnly = true), as VetRepository is
Natural-order name comparator for specialties. SpecialtyListing uses the same natural String order for specialty names, and for veterinarians compares last name, then first name
Handler shape: constructor-injected repositories, model attribute, view name under vets/. The new handler takes no page parameter and has no pagination helper
Full name rendered as first name, a space, then last name, through th:text. The empty case renders the existing #{none} key (line 21), which is the held-by-none wording
The existing place where reflection hints are registered; add the SpecialtyListing registrations beside Vet

risks.risk: Matching by instance silently lists every specialty as held by none. The specialties come from SpecialtyRepository in one session, and a vet's specialties come from the cached VetRepository.findAll() in another. They are different Java instances, and BaseEntity does not override equals, so Set.contains and equals never match.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyListing matches on the specialty identifier (docs/system-design.md § Contracts invariant; architecture-principles § Domain Core, reference by identity). The unit test builds the specialty collection and the vets' specialties as separate instances sharing an id, and the web fixture does the same.

risks.risk: Adding an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) from Specialty to its vets would create a Vet, Specialty, Vet cycle in the serialized /vets collection, and it would change the persisted mapping for a read view.
risks.mitigation: Specialty stays association-free (docs/system-design.md § Contracts invariant); SpecialtyListing derives the view in memory.

risks.risk: The grouping and ordering rules (PRD edge cases 3, 4, 5) drift into the controller as stream code, which would be a fresh Web controller violation that the recorded deviation does not cover.
risks.mitigation: The rules live only in SpecialtyListing and are unit-tested there (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; testing-principles § Test Pyramid, reviewer question on new rules). The handler reads, builds, adds to the model, and returns the view name, with no branch or sort.

risks.risk: The JVM test suite cannot observe a native-image rendering failure on a type that only the template reads reflectively (docs/system-design.md § Overview, native-image support).
risks.mitigation: Register the reflection hint in PetClinicRuntimeHints (integration point above).

risks.risk: Veterinarians are cached and specialties are not, so an out-of-band data change could make the two reads disagree (docs/system-design.md Open Question 5).
risks.mitigation: No write path exists in the application. The listing enumerates SpecialtyRepository's set, and a vet's specialty id outside it is not shown. Add no cache and no eviction in this slice.

risks.risk: Hard-coded or partly translated page wording (REQ-LANG-002), or stored names rendered as markup.
risks.mitigation: Prefer the existing keys specialties, vets, and none. Any new key lands in all eleven bundles, which I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces. Stored specialty names and veterinarian names render through th:text only, never th:utext (security-principles § Realization, cross-site scripting row).

risks.risk: The new endpoint widens the exposed surface (security-principles § Realization, widening row).
risks.mitigation: It exposes, read-only and to any caller, veterinarian names and specialty names that /vets.html already shows publicly. It offers no form and no mutation (NG-2), and management exposure is unchanged.

notes: Test placement for the prd-entry's test_names, with names used verbatim. By the testing-principles § Test Pyramid reviewer question, two names test rules that run without framework context and belong in SpecialtyListingTests: theSpecialtyListingShouldListAVeterinarianUnderEachSpecialtyTheyHold and theSpecialtyListingShouldOrderSpecialtiesAndVeterinariansAlphabetically. The other six assert the rendered page and stay in VetControllerTests on the fixed fixture described in integration_points: ...ListEverySpecialtyByStoredNameWithItsVeterinarians, ...ShowEachVeterinarianByFirstThenLastName, ...OmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty (James Carter), ...ShowAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage (no page selector), ...ShowAnUnheldSpecialtyAsHeldByNone (the unheld fixture specialty shows the none wording), and ...CarrySiteNavigationWithoutAnEntryForItself. SpecialtyListingTests may add one identifier-matching case under its own the{Subject}Should{Outcome} name. Existing tests showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList stay untouched (REQ-VET-001 unchanged). Design-doc writes: docs/system-design.md provenance header (REQ-VET-003 rows are designed, not derived), the § Contracts invariants paragraph, two new rows (SpecialtyListing, SpecialtyRepository), and REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, and VetController rows. No ADR: every pattern used is already In force, and no recorded decision is reversed. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Binding and mass assignment: the new handler binds no request data. A grep over the diff's added lines for @RequestParam|@PathVariable|@ModelAttribute|@RequestBody|setAllowedFields matched nothing; the only hits of the combined pattern were the word Runtime at diff lines 93 and 151 (PetClinicRuntimeHints). VetController.java handler `public String showSpecialtyList(Model model)` takes only the Model, so no request-bound type exists and the security-principles mass-assignment row is not engaged. Basis is grep (IntelliJ oracle not connected), the weaker basis.

XSS: every value in the new template renders through escaped th:text. specialtyList.html has `th:text="${entry.specialty.name}"` and `th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}"`. `grep -nE 'utext|\[\(|__\$\{' src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html` returned no match (exit 1), so there is no unescaped output, no unescaped inline, and no preprocessing in the new template. That matches the escaping already used for the same fields in vets/vetList.html:18 `th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}"`.

Template preprocessing: the page passes the literal 'specialties' as the layout's menu argument. fragments/layout.html:31 uses menu only in the equality `${active==menu ? 'nav-link active' : 'nav-link'}`, and its `__${link}__` preprocessing is fed only by the fixed literals at layout.html:41-57. No request-derived text reaches expression evaluation.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository adds only the derived query `Collection<Specialty> findAll()` under @Transactional(readOnly = true). No @Query, createQuery, or nativeQuery appears in the added lines (same grep, no hit). The repository is package-private and read-only, and it adds no write path (least privilege; NG-2 respected).

Widened surface: GET /specialties.html exposes, read-only and to any caller, veterinarian and specialty names that /vets.html and /vets already publish. It has no form, no mutation, and no new actuator or management exposure, and the change leaves the application no weaker than the system-design Security Context baseline.

Resource use and concurrency: the listing is bounded by the stored vet and specialty tables, not by any request input, so query parameters such as ?page=2 are ignored. It is built fresh per request. Entry copies its vet list with List.copyOf and the factory returns Stream.toList() results, so no mutable state reaches the cached Vet entities or the singleton controller, which holds only final repository fields.

Native-image hints: PetClinicRuntimeHints registers SpecialtyListing and SpecialtyListing.Entry with MemberCategory.INVOKE_PUBLIC_METHODS only. It adds no withJavaSerialization, so the unsafe-deserialization surface stays at the three existing types.

Secrets and logging: a case-insensitive grep of the diff's added lines for password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential|private.?key|jdbc: matched nothing (exit 1). The same pattern grep found no System.out or System.err in added lines, and the new handler builds no new exception messages that could reach the error page.

Supply chain: no build file is in the change set (`scripts/changeset.sh --name-only | grep -F -e build.gradle -e pom.xml -e libs.versions` exit 1). The resolved runtimeClasspath from `./gradlew dependencies` shows Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -i 'dependencycheck|owasp' build.gradle` exit 1), so no NVD match ran in this review. ./gradlew test was not run by this reviewer; the build-pass record carries the gate.
